implementation_notes: SQLAlchemy's Session is the identity map: querying the same row twice in one session returns the same object, session.identity_map is the registry keyed on the identity key, and Session.merge() first consults the local identity map before copying state. The classic structure is replaced by session lifecycle - one Session per request/unit of work (sessionmaker, scoped_session) closed at the end - rather than a hand-written dict. Two caveats matter: objects in the session are weakly referenced, so if the application drops all strong references the instance can be collected and a later load re-materialises a different object; and Django's ORM provides no equivalent, so a Django project must hand-write the map in a repository.
code_sketch:
with Session(engine) as session:
    a = session.get(Customer, 42)
    b = session.get(Customer, 42)
    print(a is b)            # True: one instance per identity
    print(session.identity_map)
    session.expunge_all()    # drop the map at unit-of-work end
pitfalls: Session objects are weakly referenced: without a strong reference (local variable, dict, session.info) an instance can be garbage-collected and the next load creates a second object.
Session is not thread-safe and must not be shared; use scoped_session or one session per request.
A long-lived session grows and serves stale data; commit/close at the unit-of-work boundary and rely on expiration/reload rather than on the map for freshness.
